case_name: Kikar Singh v State of Rajasthan
respondent:
State of Rajasthan
Supreme Court of India

12  May  1993
Cr.A. No. 437 of 1993. From the Judgment and Order Dt. 12.9.1990 of the Rajasthan High Court in D.B. Cr.A. No. 185 of 1984
The Judgment was delivered by: K. Ramaswamy, J.
1. Special leave granted.
2. The appellant was convicted under s. 302 I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life for causing the death of Jeet Singh on May 22, 1983 at about 11,00 a.m. in the field of the deceased. The Rajasthan High Court confirmed the conviction in Criminal Appeal No. 105 of 1984.
3. The case of the prosecution in nutshell was that the deceased and the appellant are neighbouring owners of lands. There was an altercation between them due to the appellant throwing soil into the lands of the deceased from 'Dali' (strip of land dividing the two fields of the deceased and the appellant). Thereon the deceased went to the appellant to persuade him not to throw the soil into their field and to have the matter settled amicably
facts: The case of the prosecution in nutshell was that the deceased and the appellant are neighbouring owners of lands.
There was an altercation between them due to the appellant throwing soil into the lands of the deceased from 'Dali' (strip of land dividing the two fields of the deceased and the appellant).

The deceased went to the appellant to persuade him not to throw the soil into their field and to have the matter settled amicably through negotiations and if need be by measuring the lands, yet the appellant was annoyed with the conduct of the deceased and his sons PW- 1 and PW-2 and son-in-law PW-3.

At the instigation of his son by name Pappu (who was a juvenile offender and was dealt with separately), the appellant inflicted with Kassi (spade, sharp edged cutting instrument) on the head of the deceased and with its impact the deceased fell down.
Thereafter the appellant inflected two more injuries.
issues: Whether the offence committed by the appellant is one of murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder?
petitioner_arguments: The contention of the learned counsel is that the appellant committed the offence on the spur of moment when quarrel ensued between the appellant and the deceased, when the appellant was prevented to spread the soil in his field.
So in heat of passion and on the spur of moment without premeditation the appellant inflicted injuries on the deceased.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution argued that the offence committed by the appellant is one of murder as it was done with intention to cause death or bodily injury which is likely to cause death.
court_reasoning: We found no infirmity in the assessment of the evidence, though the counsel for the appellant attempted to argue the case in that behalf.

The doctor found that by the third injury on the right side of the neck, the vessels on the right side of the neck were completely cut, cervical vertebra along with spinal cord were cut through larynx and also right side of mandible.
Accordingly it was held that exception 4 does not apply though there was sudden quarrel and that the fight was not premeditated to cause death.
holding: The conviction for offence under s. 302 by the High Court reversing the acquittal by trial court was upheld.
